extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic/arithmetic-geometry and anabelian geometry familiar with Mochizuki's IUT
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, assumptions, and rigidity statements for mono-theta environments and l-th roots of etale theta functions in the context of inter-universal Teichmüller theory. Focused on group-theoretic reconstruction, cyclotomic envelopes, and compatibility conditions at cusps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumption (0): X admits K-core
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume X is a smooth log-curve of type (1;1) over a field K of characteristic 0 and that X admits K-core.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This assumption is the starting hypothesis for the constructions that follow (log-structures associated to cusps, log-fundamental groups, etc.). It is required to form the exact sequences and coverings used throughout the section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumption (1): choice of quotient Q with trivial restriction on Dx
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose a quotient Q of π1^ell_X onto a free Z/lZ-module of rank 1 such that the restriction Dx → Q to the decomposition subgroup at the cusp x is trivial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This guarantees that every cusp of the chosen covering X is K-rational; it produces the covering X → X with Gal(X/X) = Q and determines associated open subgroups of arithmetic/geometric fundamental groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumption (2): element lifting nontrivial element of Gal(X=C)=Z/2Z
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose an element of Gal(X=C) = Z/2Z which lifts the nontrivial element; consider its conjugation action on π1^ell_X to obtain eigenspace decomposition (eigenvalues −1 and +1) and a direct product decomposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This choice produces the splitting π1^ell_X = π1_X^(−1) × π1_X^(+1) compatible with conjugation by π1_X and is used to define splittings Im(s_ι) etc.; uses l ≠ 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumption (3): choose sA(3) in Sect(Dx → GK)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose any element sA(3) of H^1(GK; π1^(+1)) = Sect(Dx → GK) (i.e., a section of the surjection Dx → GK) whose image is compatible with the canonical integral structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section determines a quotient and hence a covering X → X with Gal(X/X) = π1^(+1); the covering is totally ramified at cusps and plays the role of 'taking an l-th root of the theta function'. Compatibility with integral structure removes certain multiplicative indeterminacies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 7.10: smooth log-orbicurve of type (1; l-tors)
rubrics_metrics.description: A smooth log-orbicurve over K is called of type (1; l-tors) if it is isomorphic to X constructed from some choice of the quotient Q satisfying Assumptions (0) and (1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This labels the particular family of curves used to build the mono-theta/multi-theta objects; the definition ties the geometric object to the chosen arithmetic quotients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 7.11: smooth log-orbicurve of type (1; l-tors(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A smooth log-orbicurve over K is called of type (1; l-tors(2)) if it is isomorphic to X constructed under Assumptions (0), (1) and (2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This refines the type by incorporating the Z/2Z-action choice (Assumption (2)); it affects Galois properties (e.g., C → C non-Galois) and eigenspace decompositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumption (4): quotient factors through the natural Z used to define Y
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume the quotient π1^ell_X → Q factors through the natural Z discussed in the construction of Y (the intermediate quotient used when defining Y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures the covering (˜Y → X) factors as required for the later diagrammatic and cohomological arguments about theta-classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumption (5): compatibility of chosen section with f{1}-structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume the choice of an element of Sect(Dx → GK) in Assumption (3) is compatible with the {±1}-structure (f{1}-structure) referenced in Proposition 7.9 (3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compatibility implies the section respects the canonical integral structure at decomposition groups and is crucial for removing integral indeterminacies in theta-class choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of types over Q_p: (1; Z/lZ), (1; (Z/lZ)^2), (1; (Z/lZ)⋊?)
rubrics_metrics.description: A smooth log-orbicurve over a finite extension K of Q_p is called of type (1; Z/lZ) (resp. (1; (Z/lZ)(2)), resp. (1; Z/lZ)(±1)) if it is isomorphic to X (resp. X, resp. C) constructed under Assumptions (0)–(5). These deﬁnitions are made only over finite extensions of Q_p and assume residue characteristic is odd and certain Galois/field containment hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These labels distinguish variants of the basic construction depending on which torsion-extraction choices are implemented and the local field hypotheses; they also control which subsequent group-theoretic reconstructions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 7.14: standard type for l-th roots of the etale theta function
rubrics_metrics.description: An l-th root class (the cohomology class representing the l-th root of the etale theta function) is said to be 'of standard type' if the underlying class (before extracting Z_l-orbit) is of standard type (as previously defined).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The standard-type condition is a structural constraint on the theta-class used to invoke rigidity results; it is preserved under the isomorphisms discussed in the propositions and corollaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constant Multiple Rigidity of l-th Roots (Corollary 7.15 (1))
rubrics_metrics.description: An isomorphism of the relevant topological groups preserves the property that the l-th-root class is of standard type; moreover, the property determines the collection of classes up to a Z_l-multiple.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rigidity means the standard-type property is an invariant under group-theoretic isomorphism and that the ambiguity in the class is only by multiplication by elements of Z_l (a controlled constant multiple).

rubrics_metrics.name: f{1}-structure determines Z_{2l}-structure at cusps (Corollary 7.15 (2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the cusps of X are K-rational, residue characteristic of K is prime to l, and Z_l ⊂ K, then the f{1}-structure determines a Z_{2l}-structure at decomposition groups of cusps; this structure is compatible with the canonical integral structure and preserved by isomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under these arithmetic hypotheses, the additional discrete structure at cusps (lifting f{1}-structure to a 2l-structure) can be reconstructed and is invariant under the group-level isomorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 7.12 criterion: stable reduction with singular, geometrically irreducible special fiber
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume X (resp. yX) of the given type has stable reduction over O_K (resp. O_yK) whose special fiber is singular and geometrically irreducible, with the node rational. Then any isomorphism of the corresponding topological fundamental groups induces isomorphisms of many associated arithmetic/geometric fundamental groups and related structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This geometric hypothesis allows group-theoretic reconstruction of various π1-quotients (including π1^temp) and ensures compatibility of induced isomorphisms with the arithmetic actions; used to propagate local information under isomorphism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 7.16: labelling cusps determines bijection with Aut_K(X)
rubrics_metrics.description: With a labelling on cusps of X induced by labelling irreducible components of Y by Z, there is a bijection {cusps of X} = Aut_K(X) = jFℓj, and this bijection is preserved by any isomorphism of the relevant topological groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a combinatorial invariant (labelling) which is stable under the group-level isomorphisms and ties geometric automorphisms to the arithmetic labelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 7.17: cyclotomic envelope and mod N tautological section
rubrics_metrics.description: For an integer N ≥ 1, define the cyclotomic envelope (π1)[(Z/N)] := π1 ⋊ GK (with Z/N attached) and the (mod N) cyclotome ker((π1)[(Z/N)] → π1). There is a tautological mod N section GK → (π1)(Z/N;K) inducing a mod N tautological section salg: π1 → π1[(Z/N)].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This construction attaches a cyclotomic Z/N factor functorially to the topological group and supplies a canonical section used to define (Z/N)-conjugacy classes and orbits; it is foundational for the cyclotomic rigidity statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 7.18: center characterisation of kernels and compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The kernel of the natural surjection (π1)[(Z/N)] → π1 is equal to the center of (π1)[(Z/N)], and similarly for other instances; consequently any isomorphism of such cyclotomic envelopes is compatible with the canonical surjections to π1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This structural fact ensures that passing to the cyclotomic envelope is a group-theoretically recoverable operation and that isomorphisms must respect these central kernel structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 7.19: inclusion/equality about kernels and reconstructability (cyclotomic rigidity)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) There is an inclusion identifying certain kernels with the l-torsion subgroup; (2) an equality describing an intersection involving (l-torsion)[(Z/N)] and the image of the mod N tautological section. The splitting l(...) can be group-theoretically reconstructed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These group-theoretic identities come from the theta/Heisenberg group structure and imply that the cyclotomic data and the splitting can be reconstructed from the topological group, which is a key input for the cyclotomic rigidity of mono-theta environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition 7.20: mod N model mono-theta environment
rubrics_metrics.description: A mod N model mono-theta environment consists of: the topological group π1^temp_Y[(Z/N)], the subgroup D_Y := ⟨Im(K^×), Gal(Y/X)⟩ ⊂ Out(π1^temp_Y[(Z/N)]), the (Z/N)-conjugacy class of certain subgroups of π1^temp_Y[(Z/N)], and the theta section s^(N)_Y determined by the image of the chosen theta-class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A more abstract notion (mod N mono-theta environment) is any triple (π1[(Z/N)]; D; collection_of_subgroups) isomorphic to such a model; isomorphisms of mono-theta environments are isomorphisms of the underlying topological groups preserving the D-subgroup and the theta-section-conjugacy class. This package encodes the data used in rigidity theorems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 7.21: group-theoretic characterisation of the image of the tautological section and automorphism behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: The image of the tautological section (the algebraic/mod N theta section) is characterised as the intersection of (l-torsion)[(Z/N)] with a conjugation-stability condition: elements a·σ(a)^(−1) in certain automorphism-conjugates whose image in Out lies in D_Y and which induce the identity on the quotient. Moreover, automorphisms of the mod N model mono-theta environment induce automorphisms of the underlying π1^temp_Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a purely group-theoretic description of the theta-section image and shows that automorphisms of the mono-theta environment must preserve the DY-subgroup and extend to automorphisms of the full topological π1-objects. It underpins later rigidity results (cyclotomic, constant multiple, discrete).

rubrics_metrics.name: Three rigidities for mono-theta environments (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: The section announces three important rigidities for mono-theta environments: constant multiple rigidity, cyclotomic rigidity, and discrete rigidity (the latter does not hold for bi-theta environments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the principal types of invariance one can extract from the mono-theta environment package: (i) constant multiple rigidity controls multiplicative indeterminacy; (ii) cyclotomic rigidity reconstructs cyclotomic splittings; (iii) discrete rigidity gives further discrete invariants. The precise statements and uses follow in Theorem 7.23 and surrounding text.
